messages:
maya: quick question — we're re-evaluating the internal edge gateway shape. do we go REST-first with protobuf + envoy transcoding, or gRPC-first with json fallbacks? thinking about rollout UX, quotas, and telemetry.
liam: +1 on surfacing the tradeoffs. high-level: gRPC gives us smaller payloads & server-streams, but harder for ad-hoc curl/debug and for some client teams (mobile/web). REST wins for discoverability.
anita: also remember our console: quotas and per-route dashboards assume HTTP semantics today (status codes, path-based quotas). switching to gRPC will require reworking telemetry surface.
samir: curious about fallback strategy. if we do gRPC-first, can we auto-transcode on the edge to REST for downstream clients? envoy has proto->json but we lose streaming and bidi semantics.
maya: exactly. streaming loss is big for long-polling chat endpoints. but we could keep streaming on dedicated routes and use transcoding for simpler endpoints.
liam: another ops concern: routing policies. we want policy-based routing (latency vs cost). gRPC allows per-method routing granularity in xprc headers, but path based routing works too. Either way, our gateway must tag requests for cost accounting.
anita: telemetry item: need per-method token-level cost breakdown (tokens, seq len distribution). with gRPC we need to ensure our tracing headers propagate and that prometheus/gRPC labels map to console charts.
samir: on quota enforcement — we currently enforce at HTTP layer by path+api_key. gRPC enforcement needs method-level matcher in the gateway. Not hard but duplication risk with proto defs.
maya: what about developer ergonomics? proto-first forces teams to maintain .proto for every internal API; REST-first lets teams iterate faster. but proto gives strict contracts which helps rollouts.
liam: rollout UX: canary + A/B by routing % is simpler with gRPC because method signatures are stable. With REST we often do param/response evolution and need schema checks in our console.
anita: proposal: REST-first for public-ish internal endpoints (client teams), gRPC-first for backend-backend high-throughput services. gateway should support both with an explicit mapping layer and single pane telemetry.
samir: implementation note: recommend a lightweight proto registry that can be autogenerated from OpenAPI for REST endpoints. keeps single source of truth and lets us reuse envoy filters.
maya: sample quick idea for the mapping (pseudo):
```
# gateway route config
- match: POST /v1/generate
  backend: recommend-service.Generate
  proto: proto/recommend.proto#GenerateRequest
  streaming: false
```
liam: love that. Also add "quota_key: token" and "trace_key: x-request-id" so console can correlate.
ops-bot: [deploy-bot] started canary deploy of gateway v2 to eng-staging (canary=5%) :rocket:
anita: next steps: 1) spec a mapping schema for routes 2) audit our console to ensure gRPC labels accepted 3) prototype proto<->openapi generator 4) docs for teams on when to pick gRPC vs REST
maya: ok i'll spin up a short RFC with examples and a 2-week prototype plan. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
liam: happy to help on the telemetry piece.
samir: i'll pair on the proto->openapi generator.
maya: tagging @product to keep them in the loop on console changes :)
